title: Count and accumulate
ready: Read variables, integer arithmetic and selection first. Trace the accumulator before changing the loop.
task: Predict the supplied three-round example. Then complete A and B independently, recording expected results before running Python or doing a labelled hand trace.
feedback: Compare A, B and the exit with the explained key. If only the last value survives, check that initialisation is outside the loop; if n = 1 gives zero, check the excluded range stop.
retry: Close the key. Use n = 3: predict 6, trace every update and explain why the loop includes 3. Return next lesson with n = 5; predict before running.

title: Select and order records
ready: Complete activity 01 on keys and the supplied Member/Loan tables before activity 02. Practice SELECT and ORDER BY before filters, joins or groups.
task: Use this pack’s Member/Loan dataset, not the chapter’s different database. Open files/practice.sqlite OR run files/setup.sql once in a fresh SQLite database. Keep the Activity 01 tables beside you for paper practice.
feedback: Compare column order, every row and the secondary sort with the Activity 02 key. A correct-looking first row is insufficient. SELECT reads rows; it does not change stored data.
retry: Close the key. Return item and loan_id from Loan, ordered by item ascending then loan_id descending. Camera rows should be 103 then 101. Next lesson change the secondary order and explain which rows move.
scope: Unit 2 beginner SQL; grouped reports come later

title: Follow a message
ready: Know the difference between a local link and another network. Use the simplified devices and roles in the worked path; no packet capture or specialist pod is needed.
task: Draw the simplified remote-server path, then try the local-switch case and the cached-page diagnosis. Name the evidence you would request before selecting a fault.
feedback: Use the Activity 01 key to compare each forwarding responsibility. If every box is a router, relabel access, local forwarding and routing before retrying.
retry: Close the key. Change the destination to a different subnet: explain why the router is now required. Next lesson explain why a cached page alone cannot establish that DNS works.

title: Represent an unsigned value
ready: Use 8-bit unsigned values and the place weights 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1. Read the hexadecimal worked section before the mixed conversions.
read: Place value changes with the base
task: Reproduce the worked conversion of 45, then independently convert 58 and 10100110 and test the declared 8-bit boundaries. Show place-value working.
feedback: Compare both numeric value and stated width with the Activity 01 key. If hexadecimal digits are reversed, label both nibbles before converting again.
retry: Close the key. Convert 75 to 8-bit binary and hexadecimal, then check it by summing place values: 01001011 and 4B. Cover these expected results until you have attempted it. Next lesson choose a new value and explain the 255/256 boundary.
scope: Unit 1 representation; later CPU/performance activity is supporting context
